items.q: What is the AI engineer's job now, according to Dhinakaran?
items.a: Not writing the feature but **building the loop** that builds, evals, ships, monitors and improves it.

items.q: Who should consume telemetry data now?
items.a: **Agents should be the primary consumers**; observability data becomes the trigger for always-on agents.

items.q: Where should an AI engineer spend more and more time?
items.a: **Writing evals** and **aligning them with human judgment**.

items.q: What can wake an always-on agent?
items.a: A **cadence** (every 3-6 hours), an **event** like a Slack complaint, or a **metric threshold**.

items.q: What does each agent run start with?
items.a: A fresh **sandbox** with traces, logs, repo access and keys, and **a single proxy** as the only way in or out.

items.q: What persists after a run and what is torn down?
items.a: **Findings and learned skills persist in memory**; the sandbox, **credentials and repo access are removed**.

items.q: What happens if the sandbox or harness fails mid-run?
items.a: State lives outside the sandbox, so the agent **resumes from the failed step**.

items.q: Why keep the agent harness- and model-agnostic?
items.a: To **compare quality against cost** across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and different models.

items.q: How does Arize decide whether to trust a new LLM judge?
items.a: It **evaluates the evaluator** against a **golden human-labelled dataset** and ships only when they agree.
**Offline** to catch regressions before shipping and **online** on production traces.

items.q: Which agents should you trace besides your product agents?
items.a: The **coding agents that build them**: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex.
